reasons.plausibility: Cu has very low solubility in many refractory HEA matrices and tends to form embrittling phases at grain boundaries, making the claim of preserved structural integrity under cyclic loading at 600–800°C highly questionable.
reasons.testability: The test design is clear and includes a specific falsification criterion (statistically significant <20% conductivity increase or >10% strength drop), but the 500-cycle test may be insufficient to assess long-term structural integrity under service conditions.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a critical trade-off (conductivity vs. strength) with a specific, testable intervention, but the choice of Cu is problematic for high-temperature structural alloys, reducing its practical value.
